results.raw_content: [Skip to content](#universite-paris-saclay-department-of-computer-science) Admissions **The 2026 intake is closed.** Applications for the 2027 intake are expected to open in early 2027. The deadlines below are from the 2026 cycle and are kept for reference until the 2027 dates are confirmed. Fees **Non-EU students are exempt from the extra inscription fees for the 2026 inscription.** For new arrivals in 2027 this is likely to change, but nothing is confirmed yet. ## Université Paris-Saclay, Department of Computer Science[¶](#universite-paris-saclay-department-of-computer-science "Permanent link") # Artificial Intelligence Master Track[¶](#artificial-intelligence-master-track "Permanent link") One of the most selective AI master programs in France — in 2026, we received over 2,000 applications for 25 places for the full program and nearly 500 applications for the additional 5 places we offer for entry at the second year. We welcome students with a strong background in **computer science, mathematics, or physics** who want to dive deep into the mathematical foundations of modern AI and apply them to real-world problems. Our program has a distinctive focus on **Natural Language Processing**: many of the researchers who teach here are active NLP researchers at [LISN](https://www.lisn.upsaclay.fr/) and beyond, which means rich course offerings and abundant research opportunities in this area. A secondary focus is **Scientific Machine Learning** — applying ML to physics, chemistry, and the life sciences. While the program is research-oriented, many of our graduates go on to successful careers in industry. Read more about [what this master program is](admissions/what-is-this-master-program/) and [whether you should apply](admissions/should-i-apply/). Is this the right program for you? If you're passionate about the mathematics behind language models, deep learning, and data-driven science, you're in the right place. Beyond mathematics, we emphsize AI applications for language and sciences. If your primary interest is pure mathematics, consider the [M1 Mathématiques et Intelligence Artificielle](https://www.universite-paris-saclay.fr/formation/master/mathematiques-et-applications/m1-mathematiques-et-intelligence-artificielle) at Paris-Saclay. For computer vision at the M2 level, the [MVA master](https://www.master-mva.com/) is an excellent option (Note that this is a 2-year program and there is no access from our M1 to MVA — choose a different M1 if your plan is to go there). You can also explore the other tracks in the [Informatics Master](https://www.universite-paris-saclay.fr/formation/master/informatique). Access to the AI track is also highly restricted for students from other tracks, so if you want to join us, it's best to apply directly to the AI track at the M1 level. Coordinators of the AI master program: [ai.master-informatique@universite-paris-saclay.fr](mailto:ai.master-informatique@universite-paris-saclay.fr?subject=I%20am%20not%20applying%20through%20mail%20and%20I%20have%20carefully%20read%20all%20the%20AI%20track%27s%20pages%20but%20I%20still%20have%20a%20precise%20question%20that%20I%20cannot%20find%20an%20answer%20to) * **2025-26: Program Director M1 AI:** [Nona Naderi](https://perso.lisn.upsaclay.fr/wiki/en/naderi/start) * **2025-26: Program Director M2 AI:** [Kim Gerdes](https://gerdes.fr) In partnership with **Marc Evrard** and **Thomas Gerald** (M2 internship coordination) [Romane Taddei](mailto:romane.taddei@universite-paris-saclay.fr?subject=I%20am%20not%20applying%20through%20mail%20and%20I%20have%20carefully%20read%20all%20the%20AI%20track%27s%20pages%20but%20I%20still%20have%20a%20precise%20question%20that%20I%20cannot%20find%20an%20answer%20to) (pedagogical secretary) Warning Please do not email us about your individual case before having precisely studied this page, including [the page "Details about the application"](admissions/details-about-the-application/). # Application Information – 2026 Admissions[¶](#application-information-2026-admissions "Permanent link") Admissions for 2026 are closed The 2026 application deadlines (M1: March 16, M2: April 1) have passed. The dates below describe the **2026 cycle** and are kept as a reference for what the **2027 intake** will likely look like. Applications for 2027 are expected to open in early 2027; exact dates will be posted here once confirmed. ## Application Deadlines 2026[¶](#application-deadlines-2026 "Permanent link") * **M1 deadline: March 16, 2026** * **M2 deadline: April 1, 2026** For admitted students, key dates (arrival, late arrival policy, and planned end dates for M1/M2) are listed on the [After admission page](admissions/after-admission/#key-dates). It is recommended to apply once you have received **all or most of your first-semester grades**. For **M1**, the deadline is **March 16** — apply as soon as you have your grades. For **M2**, applications are reviewed in batches; there is no advantage in applying long before the **April 1** deadline. In recent years, we received **over 1,000 applications for M1** (20–30 available places) and **~400 applications for M2** (~10 available places). 👉 **Please do not email us about your individual case before having precisely studied this page, including [the page "Details about the application"](admissions/details-about-the-application/).** ### Master 1 (First Year) – 2026 Intake[¶](#master-1-first-year-2026-intake "Permanent link") 📅 **Application period:** January 15 – March 16 * **International students:** via **Inception** * **French students or those already in France:** via **Mon Master** (opens February 17) ### Master 2 (Second Year) – 2026 Intake[¶](#master-2-second-year-2026-intake "Permanent link") 📅 **Application period:** March 1 – April 1 * **Applications via Inception only** * **Requirement (M1 and M2):** *[Applicant Auto-Evaluation Form](https://forms.gle/QvcmcmXWuSdfDXYdA)* # The AI master[¶](#the-ai-master "Permanent link") The Paris-Saclay AI track of the Computer Science Master was founded in 2019 by Isabelle Guyon. It is a very selective 2-year master program with 500–1500 applicants at the first-year entry level for ~25 slots. It inherited from a previous 1-year Master 2 program run by Alexandre Allauzen. It includes a rigorous program with foundational courses and more advanced classes in machine learning, computer vision, and natural language processing. It is taught by 17 professors, including 14 Université Paris-Saclay faculty and 3 external experts. The AI master is a "parcours" (track) of the Université Paris-Saclay Computer Science (Informatique) master. It delivers a **master diploma in computer science** in 2 years, recruiting at the BAC+3 level (license or bachelor). The classes are taught in English and include: * **Foundational classes** (math, probability and statistics, signal processing, and optimization) * **Growth classes** (data science, machine learning, computer vision, and natural language processing) * **Soft skills** (e.g. Language, communication, entrepreneurship) * **Practical work** (e.g. Projects, internships, summer schools) It provides a **balance between theoretical and practical instruction**. See [CLASS LIST](classes/). [CALENDAR](time-table/) Please note that starting from 2023, we are no longer offering the AI - EIT Digital track. 📅 **Click to load the official Google Calendar (M1 & M2, with rooms)** Loading will set third-party cookies from Google Source: the [official agenda](time-table/#live-calendar) — [full agenda site](https://sites.google.com/view/mastersagenda/master-ai?authuser=0) maintained by the secretary. Ensure the evolution over time of implemented systems. ## Objectives At the Master 1 level, the objective is, on the one hand, to deepen the general training of students in Computer Science through a certain number of classic teaching units (software engineering, advanced algorithms), and on the other hand, to allow them to acquire knowledge specific to the field of the CNS and the M2 courses. Les cours suivants traitent en détail des différentes couches du réseau Internet en adoptant une approche "top-down" et en identifiant à chaque étape les enjeux et les solutions proposées. L'architecture et les protocoles point à point et multi-points de l'internet sont traités de manière approfondie avec une introduction aux réseaux ad hoc mobiles (MANET) et aux réseaux tolérants aux temps (DTN). Par ailleurs, les architectures de réseaux spécifiques aux data centres sont introduites et les spécificités de ces environnements sont mises en avant. Learning objectives L'objectif de ce cours est d'approfondir les notions de réseaux informatiques. Il suit une approche descendante des protocoles de communication, du niveau applicatif jusqu'à l'infrastructure de transmission. Au niveau de chaque couche, les mécanismes mis en jeu sont identifiés avec précision et approfondissement, ainsi que leur impact sur les performances du réseau. Ainsi, les mécanismes de contrôle de la qualité de service dans les réseaux sont identifiés et leur impact est étudié. Le cours aborde également les architectures des réseaux et des services avancés et explique leur mise en œuvre à l'aide d'outils de simulation et d'analyse de protocoles. Bibliography Jim Kurose, Computing Networking, Addison-Wesley.
